correctness.rationale: The nine displayed spherical harmonics form a basis. All 1001 ten-vertex and 364 eleven-vertex submatrices were exhaustively reduced modulo 97 and 109 under valid maps sqrt(3)->10 and 49; rank nine modulo either prime certifies rank nine over Q(sqrt(3)). The 45 modular-rank-eight ten-vertex subsets equal four disjoint octahedral orbits of sizes 6,24,12,3. Exact Q(sqrt(3)) row substitutions certify four nonzero null vectors for those orbit representatives; symmetry propagates them. Thus those sets have rank at most eight and, by modular rank eight, exactly eight. The code independently recomputes both modulus results and the exact witnesses; no floating-point or extrapolation.

value.rationale: The object is the natural 14-node spherical sampling grid given by normalized rhombic-dodecahedral vertices, with nine-dimensional quadratic harmonic bandwidth. The result gives a genuinely sharp worst-case erasure guarantee (any 11 of 14), quantifies failure among the maximally erased ten-node cases (45 of 1001), and identifies four distinct geometric configurations by exact vanishing quadrics. These exact deterministic guarantees are not equivalent to a rank check of the full node set and are useful to distinguish sampling geometry from generic sample-count bounds. Scope is intentionally finite but complete for this motivated boundary.
